newsitem.title: UK: Virgin launches new UK-Belgium air fares.
newsitem.headline: Virgin launches new UK-Belgium air fares.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson's low-cost airline Virgin Express said on Friday it would be offering a standard single fare of 32 stg exclusive of taxes on the new London-Brussels service which starts on Sunday.

It was announced earlier that Virgin Express is taking over Belgian carrier Sabena's nine daily services between Heathrow and Brussels under a wet-lease deal whereby Virgin will operate the service for Sabena using Virgin aircraft and crew.
Virgin said it is offering an introductory fare of 29 stg one-way before taxes, for purchases made by the end of October, and a standard fare of 32 stg one-way thereafter.
In comparison rivals British Midland Airways and British Airways both said on Friday that their lowest current fare on the Heathrow-Brussels route was 85 stg return exclusive of taxes.

Virgin Express was created in April with Branson's takeover of European regional carrier EuroBelgian Airlines SA for 38 million stg, with the declared aim of undercutting major operators in mainland Europe.

Before the Sabena deal came along Virgin had said the British shorthaul market was already highly competitive compared with the rest of Europe and its main target for expansion would be overpriced mainland routes dominated by national carriers.
"This deal with Sabena now allows us the opportunity to offer our low-fare, high quality service to the UK public for the first time," Branson said in a statement.
